intent: Finish low-resolution program-card icons, reusing the exact canonical Spellforge texture wherever its visual operation matches. No run layout or rules changes.
shared_prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ONE Rootward fantasy programming roguelite card icon. Style: polished high-resolution fantasy pixel art, matching the finished bronze-and-jewel icons. Bold dark plum contours, rich bronze fittings, broad cyan/amber/violet crystal planes, restrained ivory highlights, crisp stepped edges and large readable clusters. Design with roughly 128-pixel detail density, NOT an enlarged crude 32-pixel placeholder. Compact SQUARE composition, the single icon centred and filling 82 percent of both width and height, with transparent margins. Genuinely transparent alpha background. No words, letters, numerals, UI, decorative outer frame, scenery, ground, fake checkerboard, haze, tiny wires or particles. Subject:

amplify.summary: Adds 3 power to every bolt. The more bolts, the more it adds.

binary-execute.summary: For each foe, weakest first, binary-searches the sorted volley for the smallest bolt that kills it. Only those bolts fly. On unsorted data it picks wrong.

bisect-insert.summary: Binary-searches for where a 7-power bolt belongs and puts it there, twice. A sorted volley stays sorted; an unsorted one gets them wherever the search lands.

bubble-sort.summary: Walks the volley again and again, swapping neighbours that are out of order, until a pass swaps nothing: weakest first. Free, and slow, O(n²). A forge optimises it into Merge Sort.

chain-lightning.summary: Turn attacks to spark and aim them at foes in turn. Attacks already made of spark gain 2 power. Guards pass through without consuming a target.

charge.summary: Sets every bolt to spark, 1 stronger. Foes weak to spark take half again as much.

chill.summary: Sets every bolt to frost, 1 stronger. Foes weak to frost take half again as much.

dedupe.summary: A set remembers every power seen: a bolt whose power was seen before is dropped, and every bolt that stays gains 2.

divide.summary: Splits the volley in half, and each half in half, down to single bolts. Every level makes every bolt 1 stronger: about log₂ n each.

exhaustive-kill.summary: Tries every subset of the first 12 bolts to find the one that kills the front foe with the least overkill (2ⁿ subsets). The rest go at the next foe.

exhaustive-ward.summary: Tries every subset of the first ten bolts (2ⁿ of them) for the one that reaches 12 block with the least to spare. Those bolts guard you; the rest still fly. Perfect, and slow.

fib-memo.summary: The same Fibonacci surge, remembered instead of recomputed: each fib(i) is the sum of the two before it. O(n) where the naive one was O(2ⁿ).

fib-surge.summary: Each bolt gains fib(i) power for its place i in the volley (up to fib(16)), computed by naive recursion: about 2ⁿ calls. A forge can optimise it.

filter-weak.summary: Drops every bolt under 3 power; the strongest bolt that stays absorbs what was dropped. If none would stay, it keeps them all.

fire-constant.summary: Appends one 6-power fire bolt. const: stays in your hand until played, without using a hold slot.

fork.summary: Every bolt splits in two, each with 60% of its power (at least 1). The volley doubles.

frost-constant.summary: Appends one 6-power frost bolt. const: stays in your hand until played, without using a hold slot.

generator.summary: A generator that never runs out: for the rest of the fight, every program starts with two more 3-power bolts, yielded one at a time.

global-total.summary: For the rest of the fight, every program adds the damage it lands to a global total. Release turns the total into a bolt.

greedy-assign.summary: Sorts the bolts strongest first and the foes weakest first, then pours bolts into each foe until it would die. The rest go at the toughest.

greedy-ward.summary: Greedy defence: the strongest bolts become your block, biggest first, until they reach 10. The rest still fly. Quick, and it may take more than it needed.

hash-aim.summary: One pass over the foes builds a map from each element to the first foe weak to it; every bolt then looks its target up in O(1). A bolt no foe is weak to flies at the front foe.

hash-merge.summary: A hash map from element to bolt: bolts of the same element fuse into one, 1 stronger for every bolt it swallowed. Fewer, bigger bolts.

higher-order.summary: map(f, bolts): every bolt gains 1 power. It also writes two Lambdas onto your draw pile, for the next turn: free cards that run once.

huffman.summary: A min-heap: take the two weakest bolts, fuse them into one 1 stronger than both together, push it back, until three bolts remain. Huffman's greedy step; they come out weakest first.

import-bisect.summary: For the rest of the fight, every bolt a source card makes is put in its sorted place by a binary search: the volley stays sorted, weakest first, with no sort card.

import-cache.summary: For the rest of the fight, a card that already ran does no work: its answers are remembered. Memoisation, as one line.

import-collections.summary: For this fight, after each source, combine bolts sharing an element, target and guard status. Their power adds together; first-seen order is kept.

import-copy.summary: For this fight, before each strike, append a copy of the last attack bolt with half its power, rounded up. Guards are never copied.

import-heapq.summary: For the rest of the fight, every strike card is handed the volley strongest first: a heap pops the biggest bolt in turn, before each aim, for free.

import-itertools.summary: For the rest of the fight, Pairwise, Exhaustive Kill, Power Set and Exhaustive Ward cost 1 less mana: the standard library writes their loops for you.

import-math.summary: For the rest of the fight, recursion reaches further: Divide adds 2 a level instead of 1, Merge Strike's merges add 40% instead of 20%, and Recursion Tree grows a level deeper.

import-numpy.summary: For the rest of the fight, shape cards do O(1) work: the whole volley changes in one vectorised step instead of bolt by bolt.

import-operator.summary: For this fight, after each shape card, add 1 power to every attack bolt. Guard bolts keep their power.

kadane.summary: Kadane's algorithm scores each bolt as its power minus 3 and keeps a running best: the stretch of neighbouring bolts with the highest score fuses into one bolt of its whole power, 1 stronger for every bolt in it.

kindle.summary: Sets every bolt to fire, 1 stronger. Foes weak to fire take half again as much.

knapsack-strike.summary: Dynamic programming over sums: finds the smallest total a subset of bolts can make that still kills the front foe (exactly, if it can). Those fly at it; the rest at the next foe.

knapsack-ward.summary: Exhaustive Ward's question answered with a table instead of every subset: which totals can the bolts make? The smallest total of 12 or more becomes your block; the rest still fly. O(n·H), where brute force was O(2ⁿ).

lambda.summary: An anonymous function: every bolt gains 2 power. It costs nothing, and runs once.

linear-search.summary: For each foe, weakest first, checks every bolt for the weakest one that kills it alone: no sorting needed, n checks per foe. The bolts left over fly at the front foe.

lis-strike.summary: Dynamic programming finds the longest sequence of bolts that keeps rising (not necessarily neighbours): it flies at the front foe, every bolt in it stronger by the sequence's length. Every other bolt becomes block.

literal.summary: Appends one 9-power bolt: a constant written into the code, added in O(1).

load-balance.summary: Scheduling, biggest job first: each bolt, strongest first, goes to the foe with the most HP still standing after what is already aimed at it. The damage spreads evenly.

make-change.summary: Greedy change-making: the strongest bolt is paid out in coins of 5 and 1, the biggest coin that fits first, and every coin is minted 1 stronger. More bolts, and more power.

merge-sort.summary: Sorts the volley weakest first: split it in half, sort each half, merge them back. Searches need this.

merge-strike.summary: Merges the bolts in pairs, then the pairs in pairs, until one is left. Every merge adds 20%. It flies at the toughest foe.

pairwise.summary: Brute force: every pair of bolts fuses into a new bolt with their combined power, half again if their elements differ. n bolts make n(n-1)/2.

pascal-row.summary: Builds Pascal's triangle bottom-up, each entry the sum of the two above it, down to row 5, and adds that row as bolts: 1, 5, 10, 10, 5, 1.

power-set.summary: Every non-empty subset of the first three bolts, counted as a bitmask from 1 to 7, becomes one bolt of its sum. Seven bolts from three; the rest of the volley follows.

prefix-sum.summary: Each bolt becomes the running total of every bolt up to it. Totals only grow, so the volley comes out sorted.

quick-sort.summary: The first bolt is the pivot: the rest split into weaker and not weaker, and each side is sorted the same way. Weakest first, for no mana. On a volley already sorted every split is lopsided, and it slows to O(n²).

quickselect.summary: Finds the median bolt without sorting the volley: every bolt at or above it flies at the toughest foe, the rest at the weakest.

recursion-tree.summary: A function that calls itself twice, until it reaches the leaves, grows a tree three levels deep: one 5-power bolt at the root, two 4s, four 3s, added after the volley.

recursive-mirror.summary: Append a reversed copy of the volley at half power, rounded up. Recursion visits each bolt once; elements, targets and guards are copied.

reduce.summary: Folds the whole volley into one bolt: the sum of every power, plus a tenth. It takes the strongest bolt's element.

release.summary: Appends one bolt of half the fight's global total (the damage every program landed since `global total` was imported), then the total starts again from 0. Without the global, nothing.

repeat.summary: Copies the last bolt three more times (three 4-power bolts when the volley is empty). Put your strongest bolt last before it.

reverse.summary: Turns the volley around, the last bolt first. A sorted volley comes out strongest first.

round-robin.summary: Deals the bolts out to the foes in turn, like cards: the first foe, the second, the third, the first again.

run-length.summary: Combine adjacent bolts with the same element, target and guard status. Add their powers.

salvo.summary: Adds a rising run of six bolts, 1 to 6 power, after the volley.

sliding-window.summary: Each bolt gains the power of the previous two bolts. Uses the original powers and a rolling sum; keeps elements, targets and guards.

spark-constant.summary: Appends one 6-power spark bolt. const: stays in your hand until played, without using a hold slot.

split.summary: Divides every bolt of 4 or more power into its two halves, and those halves again, until every piece is under 4. The same power in many more bolts: what Amplify likes best.

stable-partition.summary: Move attack bolts of at least 6 power to the front. Keep the relative order in both groups. Sets up strong opening hits without sorting.

sweep.summary: Area: every bolt hits every foe, at half its power (at least 1).

tabulate.summary: Bottom-up dynamic programming: each bolt becomes the best total collectable up to it without taking two neighbours. The table only grows.

take-max.summary: Keeps only the three strongest bolts and makes each half again as strong. Focus beats volume. Comes out weakest first.

two-pointers.summary: On a sorted volley, one pointer at each end: the weakest and the strongest bolt fuse, then the next pair inward. Half as many bolts, all of about the same power.

ward.summary: Finds the strongest bolt and turns it into block for you, 2 stronger. The rest still fly.

zip-ward.summary: Split each attack into an attack of half power (rounded up) and a guard of half power (rounded down). Existing guards pass through.
